newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria budget deficit down in first half of April.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria budget deficit down in first half of April.

text.p: Bulgaria's central government budget deficit fell by seven billion levs in the first half of April to 291 billion levs, a Finance Ministry official said, quoting preliminary figures.
"The deficit stood at 291 billion levs on April 17," the official, who declined to be named told Reuters.
The fall in the deficit was mainly due to increased receipts from tax payments for the fiscal 1996 and the first quarter of this year, the official said.
The Finance ministry made a total of 88.438 billion levs interest and discount payments on government securities in the first half of April, Finance ministry figures showed.

The deficit at mid-April was around 1.4 percent of the nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for 1997 assumed in a funding arrangement between the interim government and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) sealed in March.
Under the arrangement the budget deficit for this year was assumed at 3.8 percent of projected nominal GDP set at 20.743 trillion levs, down a real 4.8 percent from 1996.

Figures for spending, revenue and deficit as percentage of budget targets were not available because a viable budget for 1997 has yet to be passed by the new parliament due to assemble for the first time on May 7.
Under a stop-gap budget bill approved on January 31 the deficit was limited to the amount of interest and discount payments on treasury paper.
